title.narrative: Life-saving Sexual and Reproductive Health and Gender-based Violence Interventions for Vanuatu Earthquake Response

description.narrative: UNFPA’s six-month project aims to provide integrated GBV and SRH services to reach women and girls most affected by the Earthquake that struck Vanuatu in December 2024. Through the Health and Justice, Gender and Protection Clusters, the project aims to ensure zero preventable maternal deaths and continuity of access to Family Planning and GBV multi-sectoral services during the acute and early recovery phase of the emergency for 2475 women and girls and 200 men and boys, including 860 pregnant women in Efate. Interventions will directly target displaced women and girls and host communities/families most affected by the Earthquake, particularly in the Port Vila area, contributing to their ability to access humanitarian services as well as by supporting the restoration and strengthening of SRH and GBV services for the broader population in this area, indirectly reaching an estimated 16,500 women of reproductive age.The project will implement components of the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for Reproductive Health in Emergencies. The MISP is a set of priority lifesaving interventions that are required to respond to sexual reproductive health needs at the onset of any humanitarian emergency to prevent excess sexual and reproductive health-related morbidity and mortality. Four of the six component of the MISP will be addressed through CERF funding:1. Prevent sexual violence and respond to the needs of survivors2. Prevent the transmission of and reduce morbidity and mortality due to HIV and other STIs3. Prevent excess maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality4. Prevent unintended pregnanciesDue to pre-crisis limited access to midwifery services in Efate island, a key intervention will be to provide trained and experienced midwives, who will act as the front-liners to deliver the activities to implement these MISP components in partnership with the Ministry of Health, as well as the Vanuatu Family Health Association.In line with the inter-agency Minimum Standards for GBV in Emergencies, the project will support survivors to continue to access life-saving services through the provision of Women Friendly Space (WFS) services targeting at risk women and girls. This intervention reduces barriers to access information about humanitarian assistance, and SRH and GBV services and referrals are provided in a structured place where women and girls physical and emotional safety is respected through processes of empowerment. Women and girls in all their diversity can seek, share and obtain information about services, express themselves, enhance psychosocial wellbeing and more fully realise their rights. Integrated service modalities will achieve these outcomes across Health and Protection sectors, with trusted and trained mid-wives and pre-existing networks of youth advocates and GBV service providers in Vanuatu as facilitators of access to health centre entry points and WFS. Health Mobile outreach will integrate GBV, while GBV/Gender/Protection Outreach will integrate SRH, to bring services for at risk communities closer to them.
